conventions.convention: The continuum body is Ω = ∏(0,L_i) in three-dimensional Euclidean space, with positive side lengths in metres, an open time interval in seconds, and strictly positive temperature in kelvins. Temperature has continuous first time and second spatial derivatives extending to the boundary.

Heat flux along a unit vector n is positive in direction n; face normals are outward. Insulation means j_Q·n = 0, and the adopted balance is ∂_t u + div j_Q = 0. Flux and its first spatial derivatives extend continuously to every compact time slab through the boundary.
Fourier flux is j_Q = −K∇T. Only the symmetric part K_s = (K + Kᵀ)/2 is assumed positive semidefinite; K need not be symmetric.
The continuum entropy density is adopted through s′(T) = c(T)/T, with c = u′ > 0. Its volume integral is this continuum model's entropy; it is not identified with kinetic entropy.

The constant-coefficient heat branch assumes Countable Choice, c,k > 0, a = k/c, and positive even 2L_i-periodic C² initial data whose derivatives through order two are bounded and uniformly continuous. The initial time derivative is interpreted from the right.

The kinetic collision measure is a nonnegative sigma-finite Borel measure on the elastic collision set, invariant under separate incoming and outgoing particle exchanges and incoming/outgoing pair exchange.

Incoming molecular chaos is a one-sided factorization assumption. The weak collision identity has factor 1/4, while the kinetic equation is adopted as an equality of locally integrable functions almost everywhere on the product domain.

Kinetic entropy is −k_B times the integral of f log(f/f_ref), with a positive constant reference density having the same units as f. The theorem additionally requires pointwise absolutely convergent weak identities for tests 1 and log(f/f_ref), and the stated entropy, transport, domination and spatial production integrability.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice and the stated constant positive c,k and positive even-periodic C² initial-data hypotheses. The Gaussian convolution T(x,t) = ∫ Γ(x−y,at)g(y) dy, with T(x,0) = g(x), is the unique solution in the stated boundary and initial-time regularity class of c∂_tT = kΔT with homogeneous Neumann faces. It preserves T_min ≤ T ≤ T_max and has right initial derivative aΔg.

A rectangular local-equilibrium field record consists of the stated positive-temperature field on the closed rectangle and open time interval, u ∈ C¹ on its temperature interval, and positive volumetric heat capacity c(T) = u′(T); it may also include the specified heat-flux and conductivity fields. The Definition adopts no balance or constitutive law.
For the specified regular flux records, adopt ∂_t u(T(x,t)) + div j_Q(x,t) = 0 and j_Q·n = 0 on every face.
For d ≥ 1, positive L_i, and w ∈ C¹ on the closed rectangle with ∫_Ω w = 0, ∫_Ω |w|² ≤ (d/2)∑ L_i²∫_Ω |∂_i w|² ≤ C_Ω∫_Ω |∇w|², where C_Ω = (d/2)max_i L_i².

Assume Countable Choice and the hypotheses and solution of pthm-td-constant-conductivity-neumann-existence. The spatial mean is constant and E(t) ≤ exp(−2at/C_Ω)E(0) for t ≥ 0, where E(t) = ∫_Ω |T−T̄(t)|² and C_Ω = (3/2)max_i L_i².

Adopt incoming-pair factorization, the stated absolutely convergent weak collision identity for almost every (x,t), and ∂_t f + v·∇_x f = Q_ν(f) as an equality of locally integrable functions almost everywhere on the product domain; these are model admissibility conditions, not an existence assertion.

concerns.concern: Proof 1.1 says 'The hypotheses match [L1]' and invokes thm-tdmath-regular-collision-entropy for the derivative identity at each time. The supplier assumes the kinetic equation without an almost-everywhere qualification and substitutes it at fixed time. Here [A1] imports only the equation 'almost everywhere' on the full space–velocity–time product. [A3] strengthens the weak identities to every (x,t), but does not similarly strengthen the kinetic equation. Fubini supplies the equation on almost every time slice, not every prescribed time. No continuity of Q_ν(f), or argument upgrading the production identity through exceptional times, is supplied. This leaves the unrestricted timewise derivative identity and its equality characterization unsupported by the cited interface. I have not established a counterexample; the owning group should resolve the exact equation interpretation or prove the missing extension.

seams_checked.note: The supplier page and concave-entropy postulate adopt macroscopic entropy rather than derive it. The continuum page and local caloric postulate faithfully describe their density relation as an additional adopted extension, without inferring Fourier flux, equilibration or microscopic entropy identification.

Checked both page summaries. The consumer explicitly treats this as a track prerequisite and makes no item-level deduction from Pfaff geometry. It does not promote local integrating factors into global entropy or identify horizontal curves with physical adiabatic processes.

The elastic collision definition and entropy-production formula, sign, factor 1/4, integrability requirements and restricted equality branch are reproduced faithfully. However, the H-theorem application's claim that all hypotheses match leaves the supplier's kinetic-equation requirement unmatched at exceptional time slices: the consuming postulate states only product-almost-everywhere equality. See the concern on pthm-td-collision-h-theorem. Neither page claims a microscopic derivation or uses the Maxwellian branch.
